Under explicitly listed heuristics, a complete attack executes $2^{127.5}$ instructions for BLS12-381 and $2^{103.2}$ for the BN254 curve used in Ethereum, with success probability above $0.998$. For BLS12-381 this is $9.6$ bits below Pollard's rho on the curve counted the same way, where operation counts suggested one bit: the target group is clearly the weaker side. It is also $9.8$ bits below what the published design costs when it is completed with standard components and charged in full ($2^{137.3}$ instructions, level with rho). For BN254 our figure confirms the accepted level and gives it a concrete meaning.
The method rests on three ideas and on a systematic reduction of the work per sieved cell. First, a twisted tower: a unit $c$ of the sextic base field with $c\,\sigma(c)=-1$ turns the usual sign symmetry into a symmetry of order four that acts as a Frobenius power, so that relations and ideals come in orbits of four and the linear system has Gaussian-integer entries. Second, counting each relation once: coefficient-cube estimates count unit multiples of a relation as distinct; for the published BLS12-381 design only $2^{-2.8}$ of the counted relations are distinct, and we sieve a fundamental domain instead. Third, a sieve organised around reuse: only the harder side is sieved, tiny primes are handled by batch arithmetic, and the hits of a prime ideal are replayed from lists shared by all slices. A product-form linear algebra and a planned descent complete the method. Each technique is stated for a general special pair of tower shape $(6,2)$ and then instantiated on the two curves. Nothing was run at full size; the final designs assume up to $2^{112}$ bytes of storage, which the cost model does not charge; and the practical security of both curves is unchanged.

item.title: γ₁₁: Unequal Triangles and Adapted References — the macadamia 0050
item.description:
Paper: 2026/2849
Authors: Rémi Géraud-Stewart, David Naccache
Summary: This paper settles the ninth of the ten macadamias of the series on the Hermite constant in dimension 11: the perfect form $P$ = 0050:024468269 of rank 9, of determinant 8192/9 at minimum 4. The root paper reduces $\gamma_{11}$ to chains $L\supset M\supset N$ of lattices of ranks 11, 10, 9, each with minimum at least 4; we prove that every admissible chain whose rank-9 member is admissibly marked by $P$ has $\det L\ge 972$. No argument at rank 10 can do this, because an actual lattice of rank 10 with determinant $3328/3<4\cdot 972^{9/11}$ lies over $P$. The proof is computer-assisted, with explicit finite checks. Its decisive step is elementary: the three additive dual vectors of a section covector and the first normal usually have different lengths, and keeping the three lengths in the circle obstruction, instead of their maximum, gives a determinant cap that sharpens every subsequent contact and spectral bound. Adapted reference forms turn the contact conditions into exact rational tests, a common slack is retained throughout, and four computational results reduce the problem to a five-parameter root, exhausted by a finite cover of 6 993 terminal regions replayed in exact arithmetic.

item.title: γ₁₁: One Selected Contact, Two Linked Blocks — the macadamia 0030
item.description:
Paper: 2026/2830
Authors: Rémi Géraud-Stewart, David Naccache
Summary: This paper is one of five companion papers completing the proof of $\gamma_{11}=4/\sqrt[11]{972}$ announced in the root paper and assembled in “A Focus on Hermite Constant 11”. The root paper reduces a lattice of rank 11 with minimum 4 and determinant below 972 to a chain of sections of ranks 11, 10 and 9 whose rank-9 member is admissibly marked by one of 4 487 813 perfect forms; ten of them, the macadamias, lie under an actual lattice of rank 10 and need proofs of their own. We settle the first, the form 0030:030301719 of $\Lambda_9$ under $\Lambda_{10}$, where the bound has little margin. The argument selects one contact of the reference lattice from the actual metric, keeps the off-diagonal column shared by two eight-dimensional blocks of the section metric, applies one determinant–trace theorem to both blocks, and closes with a rational cover of three scalar parameters. The proof is computer-assisted: its finite inputs are three outer-range covers, two middle-range covers with 10 498 and 1 140 leaves, an annulus tree with 3 567 leaves and four smaller trees, every leaf checked in exact rational arithmetic.

item.title: γ₁₁: Reduction by Sections — the macadamias 0019 and 0017
item.description:
Paper: 2026/2829
Authors: Rémi Géraud-Stewart, David Naccache
Summary: The root paper of this series reduces the value $\gamma_{11}=4/\sqrt[11]{972}$ of the Hermite constant in dimension 11 to a statement about chains $L\supset M\supset N$ of lattices of ranks 11, 10 and 9 whose rank-9 member lies over one of 4 487 813 perfect forms of rank 9; the $\gamma_{11}$ paper settles all of them but ten, the macadamias. This paper settles two of the ten: 0019:030884313 (the form $P_S$ of the root paper, an extension of $E_8$ by a simplex vector) and 0017:001746552 (the form $P_K$, KAPPA9.2). We prove that every admissible chain whose rank-9 member is admissibly marked by the form has $\det L\ge 972$. The method is a reduction by sections: for 0019 the nine simplex contacts turn the problem into one about an eight-dimensional covariance matrix, and a tree of 17 347 nodes with 7 743 scalar determinant witnesses covers the remaining box; for 0017 a two-vector flag bound and the decomposition of the section metric along a short-dual plane and its rank-seven kernel reduce the problem to five parameters, covered by a tree of 3 010 595 nodes. The proof is computer-assisted: every finite check is stated as a Computational result, and the verification records in the certificate archive are named.

item.title: γ₁₁: A Finite Spectral Relaxation — the macadamia 0008
item.description:
Paper: 2026/2828
Authors: Rémi Géraud-Stewart, David Naccache
Summary: The root paper of this series reduces $\gamma_{11}=4/\sqrt[11]{972}$ to a statement about chains of lattices $L\supset M\supset N$ of ranks 11, 10 and 9, cut along shortest dual vectors, whose rank-9 member lies over one of 4 487 813 perfect forms. Ten of these forms, the macadamias, lie under an actual lattice of rank 10 of small determinant and need a proof at rank 11, where the bound 972 is attained. This paper settles the form 0008:022143116, which lies under a section of $K_{11}$ with 276 minimal vectors: every admissible chain whose rank-9 member is admissibly marked by this form has $\det L\ge 972$. In coordinates aligned with the form, the section metric is $S=I+E$ with three blocks of size three. Two sufficient flag tests come from short dual covectors and integral triangles; local reductions, proved from rational comparisons and Bernstein or Sturm certificates, remove explicit regions of the parameters; every remaining real spectrum is mapped, with explicit allowances, into a finite relaxation on 81 grid nodes, which a tree of 400 nodes with 1 091 rational certificates, replayed in two exact arithmetic implementations, excludes. The proof is computer-assisted, with explicit finite checks stated as one Computational result.

item.title: γ₁₁: Contact Geometry — the macadamias 0001, 0014, 0059 and 0015
item.description:
Paper: 2026/2827
Authors: Rémi Géraud-Stewart, David Naccache
Summary: The root paper of this series reduces the value $\gamma_{11}=4/\sqrt[11]{972}$ of the Hermite constant to a statement about chains of lattices $L\supset M\supset N$ of ranks 11, 10 and 9 whose rank-9 member lies, in the sense of Voronoi, over one of 4 487 813 perfect forms; the $\gamma_{11}$ paper excludes all of them but ten, the macadamias. This paper settles four macadamias, the forms 0001:010488327, 0014:001749549, 0059:016902802 and 0015:030291998, by one method: the geometry of the contacts of the form. A section frame of short dual vectors forces the first gluing of $M$ over $N$ to lie near one of finitely many coherent centres; at such a centre the rank-10 metric is compared with an explicit reference lattice, whose Delaunay cells and contact identities give a uniform bound on its covering radius; and a primitive-extension inequality turns that bound into $\det L\ge 972$. The proof is computer-assisted: every finite check it uses is stated as a Computational result with the records of the certificate archive that certify it, and all comparisons are between explicit rational numbers.
